Pt@WS2 exhibited a robust stability with only 4 mV increment in overpotential at 100 mAcm−2 within 5000 potential cycles. The ESA value was 114.9 m2gPt−1... Pt@WS2 sustained its HER performance within 100 h.

nodes.description: Temperature-dependent HER testing for activation energy
nodes.source_text: In order to analyze the robust HER catalytic activity, HER performance was tested under various temperatures (Figure S6); therefore, the activation energy was calculated to 12.0 kJmol−1 and 13.3 kJmol−1 for Pt@WS2 and Pt/C (Figure 3c), respectively.

nodes.description: pH-dependent HER testing for reaction order
nodes.source_text: The HER catalytic activity of Pt@WS2 was more sensitive to H+ concentration (Figure 4c)... Moreover, the reaction order (ρ) was 1.8... The plot of hydrogen adsorption peak potential vs. pH was shown in Figure 4e... the slope was estimated to 17.1 mVpH−1 for Pt@WS2 explicating a 7e−/2H+ process.

In situ Raman spectroscopy was invited to visualize the hydrogen spillover during HER catalysis... the E2g peak was negatively shifted with overpotential increased to 40 mV... with the emergence of Pt-H bond at 2165 cm−1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure WS2 shows (002) facet at 14 degrees. Pt deposition results in peaks at 46 and 68 degrees, assigned to (200) and (220) planes, confirming metallic Pt nanoparticle formation without damaging the WS2 structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pure WS2 exhibited strong diffraction peak at 14° assigned to (002) facet ... the formation of Pt nanoparticle on WS2 was determined by diffraction peaks at 46° and 68° confirmed as (200) and (220) crystal planes

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f spectra show metallic Pt and Pt2+ species; W 4f peaks confirm a 2H-WS2 hexagonal structure. Negative shift in W 4f and presence of more Pt2+ moieties indicate strong electronic interplay between S and Pt atoms.
